response: **What we’re going to do** We’ll bump your Next.js app to the current stable releases. Because you’re not a developer, I’ll walk you through every tiny step and give you the exact clicks/commands you need to run in Cursor. I’ll use the safety habits you asked for: - Create a **save point** before making any changes (so you can undo if something breaks). - Keep all secret keys in `.env` (or Cursor Secrets) and never put them in the frontend. - Run the automated **secret/Spending‑cap scanner** after the upgrade so you can see any new risks. If you’re working in **Cursor’s web UI** (the normal “Code” tab) just paste the code snippets below in the correct files, then click the little “Run” button in the terminal panel. --- ## 1️⃣ Make a baseline save point 1. Open the **Terminal** in Cursor (the black “Terminal” pane at the bottom). 2. Run the quick save‑point command (Cursor uses Git under the hood): ```bash # This will make a git commit named “Before Next.js upgrade” git add . git commit -m "Before Next.js upgrade" ``` > If you see a warning that you don’t have a repo, click **“Create git repo”** and Git will > initialize one automatically. ✨ *You now have a safety net—you can go back to this state at any time.* --- ## 2️⃣ Check the current version of Next.js 1. Open `package.json` (in the left‑hand file list). 2. Look for the line `"next": "13.x.x"` – that’s your current version. 3. Open the browser and go to . 4. Read the “Upgrade to 14.0.0” notes (they’re short; just skim “Breaking changes” and “New features”). *If any of the breaking changes applies to your code (e.g., you used the old `next/image` props), we’ll handle it in step 4.* --- ## 3️⃣ Update the package lock 1. In the terminal, run: ```bash # Update the next package to the latest major release npm install next@latest --save ``` > This will also update types for React (`react`, `react-dom`) if required. 2. Wait for the terminal to finish. You’ll see “added X packages” at the end. --- ## 4️⃣ Fix any obvious breaking changes 1. **Search for "next/image"** in your code: ```bash # Find all uses of next/image grep -R "next/image" -n . ``` *If you don’t see any hits, skip to the next section.* 2. If you do see a hit, look at the file. The old syntax was like: ```tsx import Image from 'next/image' ``` 3. The new syntax requires the `width` and `height` to be *numeric* (not strings) and is optional if you use Tailwind. Keep the same `width`/`height` values, or change them to numbers if they were strings. 4. If you’re using dynamic image imports (e.g. `src={process.env.ASSET_URL + '/foo.png'}`), update those to use the new `next/image` loader rules. For most people, just giving it a static value works. 5. **Search for “`Link href=`**. New Next.js requires a `legacyBehavior` or updated `prefetch` setting if you’re using it. The easiest upgrade is just add: ```tsx // Example of the updated link import Link from 'next/link' About ``` Or, if you prefer the new API: ```tsx About ``` --- ## 5️⃣ Run the dev server and look for errors ```bash # Start the local dev server npm run dev ``` 1. In the terminal, watch the output. 2. Open your browser at . 3. If you see a red error screen, copy the stack trace and row numbers (you’ll paste it back here if you need help). Usually it will point to the file you need to edit next. --- ## 6️⃣ Run the safety scanner In the same terminal tab, run: ```bash # Scan for leaked keys, missing env prefixes, and new paid‑service costs python3 . --report upgrade-report.md ``` > Replace `` with wherever the seatbelt tool sits. > If you don’t have Python, simply skip this step—just read the repo’s `README` for > any obvious secrets (e.g., anything printed in the console). Open `upgrade-report.md` and look for: - **"Secret key found in frontend"** → Move it to a server‑only file (`/api/…`). - **"Unnecessary env prefix"** → Trim the prefix. - **"Paid‑service cost increased"** → Check if you’re calling that service in a loop. If you find any issues, jot them down; we’ll tackle them in the next step. --- ## 7️⃣ Commit the upgraded version 1. In the terminal: ```bash git add package.json yarn.lock package-lock.json git commit -m "Bump Next.js to latest version" ``` > If you used Yarn, replace `yarn.lock` instead. --- ## 8️⃣ Test all main features Let’s try the core parts of your site: 1. **Home page** – should load without errors. 2. **Images** – verify they render (look for broken image icons). 3. **Navigation links** – click to ensure they work. 4. **Forms or any API routes** – submit them and observe the console for errors. If any part breaks, share the error text and we’ll go back to the code. --- ## 9️⃣ Final safety check Once all tests pass: 1. Run the sponsor “secret” scan again to confirm nothing leaked. 2. Optional: Run the **live‑site check** (if you already have a deployed slot): ```bash python3 https://your-staging-domain.com \ --report live-check.md ``
